title: ATTACH district scoping promised in map.odin/demo/tests but implemented as explicitly global; per-district pool machinery is production-dead
evidence:
+// board: the ATTACH family draws from the anchor's OWN district's pool (an
+// estate never crosses a district boundary), and the derived cluster view is
+// unchanged (radius adjacency) — the district scoping at the DRAW makes
+// cross-district estates unreachable by construction. The exact interplay is
+// documented in growth.odin.
--- vs ---
+// The ring is GLOBAL (not district-scoped): the estate forms on the streets
+// the grid gives it — a street crossing a district's Voronoi boundary keeps
+// its houses together (the streets-rule interplay, documented in the header);
+// the seed's district labels the estate.
--- and the scan body has no district filter: ---
+	for k in 0..<len(board.candidates) {
+		c := board.candidates[k]
detail: map.odin's header, the dublin demo comment, and the test header all promise district-scoped ATTACH; the ring scan never reads candidate_district/district_start, so those fields are write-only in production and the documented invariant is unenforced.
recommended_fix: Pick one contract: filter ring candidates by the anchor's district (candidate_district + district_start), or delete the per-district fields and correct the map.odin/demo/test comments to match the global ring.

title: test_board deletes string-literal district names — freeing static data
evidence:
+	append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = "A", pos = {6, 6}})
+	append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = "B", pos = {24, 6}})
--- vs the destroy: ---
+test_board_destroy :: proc(b: ^Map_Board) {
+	delete(b.candidates)
+	delete(b.candidate_district)
+	delete(b.district_start)
+	for d in b.districts {
+		delete(d.name)
+	}
+	delete(b.districts)
+}
--- the loader clones precisely to make names deletable: ---
+		append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = strings_clone(name, allocator), kind = kind, pos = {f32(px), f32(py)}})
detail: "A"/"B" are static string literals; delete(d.name) frees them through the context allocator — invalid free/UB. The loader clones names exactly so map_board_destroy can delete them.
recommended_fix: In test_board, clone the names (e.g. strings.clone("A", context.allocator)) or stop deleting d.name in test_board_destroy.

title: map_board_destroy frees cloned strings via the destroy-time context, not the loader's allocator
evidence:
+map_board_destroy :: proc(b: ^Map_Board) {
+	for d in b.districts {
+		delete(d.name)
+	}
+	delete(b.districts)
+	delete(b.attribution)
--- strings are cloned with the caller's allocator: ---
+	b.attribution = strings_clone(attr, allocator)
--- tests load with temp_allocator then destroy under the default context: ---
+	b, err := map_board_load(transmute([]u8)src, &bal, context.temp_allocator)
+	defer map_board_destroy(&b)
detail: Dynamic arrays carry their allocator; strings do not. map_board_destroy's string deletes go through whatever context.allocator is current — mismatched free when the board was loaded with a custom allocator (both tests do).
recommended_fix: Have map_board_destroy take the board's allocator (stored on Map_Board at load) and free name/attribution through it.

title: map_test header claims district-containment and E31 pins that the tests never assert
evidence:
+//   (d) dublin growth spawns land ON the pool (a real-street tile), the E31
+//       predicates still gate (never an illegal placement), and the ATTACH
+//       family stays WITHIN the anchor's district (the growth_groups
+//       interplay: cluster radius/caps apply within districts);
--- the actual assertions are pool membership, grid bounds, radius only: ---
+		testing.expectf(t, on_pool, "attach spawn %v is NOT on a pool tile", pos)
+		// the E31 floor still holds (the existing predicate — belt)
+		testing.expectf(t, pos[0] >= 0 && pos[0] < board.w_tiles && pos[1] >= 0 && pos[1] < board.h_tiles,
detail: No test asserts district membership of attach spawns, and the comment labeled "the E31 floor" checks only grid bounds, not node/pipe separation. The header advertises coverage that does not exist.
recommended_fix: Either add the district-membership and min-separation assertions, or rewrite pin (d) to state what is actually checked (pool membership + radius).

title: map_board_load error paths discard the partially-built board, leaking its allocations
detail: Errors after districts/candidates/render_dots/district_start are allocated return {} — the backing stores are unreachable. App and harness callers discard the failed result without destroy.
recommended_fix: On every error return, call map_board_destroy(&b) first (or return the partial board to the caller for cleanup).

title: Claimed exit/teardown frees are absent from the diff (board + render cache leak)
evidence:
+	// (loaded once at boot, freed at exit) and shared with the sim + the
--- and ---
+// dublin_render_destroy — free the cache's buffers (called by view teardown).
detail: Both resources are new fields, so the frees would be new code — yet no hunk calls map_board_destroy from app/main.odin, and dublin_render_destroy is only called from dublin_render_ensure's rebuild path.
recommended_fix: Add the exit free (map_board_destroy(&app.board) when board_ok) and call dublin_render_destroy in the view teardown, or drop the comments.

title: Label collision gaps documented as world px but compared against screen-space anchor distances
detail: s.x/s.y are post-transform screen pixels; gap is a world-px constant applied unscaled. Equivalent only at scale==1 — collision behavior silently changes with zoom while label size scales.
recommended_fix: Scale the gap by v.scale at the comparison (gap * v.scale), or document the gaps as screen px at fit zoom.

title: view.odin calls the dublin cache a "triangulation cache"; the renderer rasterizes even-odd and no triangulator exists
evidence:
+	// only READS it, ODN-1); map_draw branches on them. `dublin` is the
+	// render-side triangulation cache (dublin.odin), rebuilt when the board
--- vs ---
+// no transcendentals, no libm). The terrain rasterization (even-odd
+// point-in-polygon into a per-world-px cell grid) runs ONCE per board
--- and map_ring_clean cites a triangulator the renderer never runs: ---
+// closing/stitch vertex; an ear-clip triangulator needs a simple ring), drop
detail: dublin.odin deliberately avoids ear clipping (OSM pinch artifacts); view.odin's "triangulation cache" and map_ring_clean's ear-clip rationale describe a design that was replaced.
recommended_fix: Update the view.odin comment to "rasterization cache" and reword map_ring_clean's rationale (simple ring for the fill, not for a triangulator).

title: map_board_pool_lo / map_board_pool_hi are never called
detail: No call site anywhere in the diff; growth_board_seed_draw indexes board.candidates directly. Pure dead code.
recommended_fix: Delete both accessors (and their comment), or use them in growth_board_seed_draw.

title: growth_board_ring_scan ignores its `t: ^Topology` and `alloc` parameters
detail: The body touches neither t nor alloc — the scan is a pure function of board/anchor/sep/radius, and the default alloc param is never used for appends.
recommended_fix: Drop both parameters (and update the three call sites), or use them.

title: district_start zero-fill loop is a no-op (make already zeroes)
detail: make zeroes the buffer; the loop writes 0 over 0 and its own comment admits it does nothing ("filled below"). Dead instructions obscuring the real prefix-sum below.
recommended_fix: Delete the loop; keep only the make and the counting/prefix-sum pass.

title: board_district_at duplicates the loader's inline nearest-district scan and is production-dead
evidence:
+board_district_at :: proc(board: ^Map_Board, pos: [2]i32) -> u16 {
+	best: u16 = 0
+	bd2 := max(f32)
--- the loader keeps its own inline copy instead of calling it: ---
+		best: u16 = 0
+		bd2 := max(f32)
--- and the comment acknowledges the drift hazard: ---
+// assignment exactly (same strict-less comparison + best init 0) — a
detail: Only the test calls board_district_at; the loader re-implements the identical loop. The "MUST mirror exactly" comment documents the drift risk instead of eliminating it by sharing.
recommended_fix: Have map_board_load call board_district_at (single source of truth), or delete the proc and let the test reuse the loader's path.

title: dublin-shot prints usage() on bad args but keeps executing
detail: After printing usage the handler falls through and runs anyway with rest[0], silently ignoring the extra arguments instead of exiting.
recommended_fix: Exit after usage() (e.g. usage(); os.exit(2)), matching an argument-error contract.
